subject: Renewal check-in: projected 3x usage growth & term-flex proposal
messages:
From: Sanjay Mehra <sanjay@starlift.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <procurement@starlift.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Usage spike ahead of renewal — quick sync?

Hey Lauren,

Quick one — our product team just flipped a new multimodal feature into beta and we're already seeing a ~3x uplift in token consumption this month vs Q1 averages. Renewal's coming up in ~45 days and procurement asked me to validate capacity/price options early so we don't get surprised.

Can you help with:
- a short breakdown of current token mix (prompt vs completion) and per-route latency impact
- options for smoothing sudden surges (burst credits vs committed uplift)
- any recommendations to keep unit costs down without reverting quality (caching, quantized model variants)

If useful I can run a short demo of the new flow — but for now a short health/readout would help procurement.

Thanks,
Sanjay
Sanjay Mehra
Head of Product, Starlift AI
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Mehra <sanjay@starlift.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Maya Patel <procurement@starlift.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Usage spike ahead of renewal — quick sync?

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the heads up and congrats on the beta flip. I've pulled an initial usage snapshot and attached a short report (starlift_q2_usage_report_2028.pdf). High-level findings: 

- Consumption: month-to-date tokens are ~3.1x of your trailing 30-day average; 72% of the growth is prompted by the new multimodal inference route (/vision-annotate + chat-combine).
- Mix: Prompt tokens now account for ~41% of total tokens (was 22% previously); completions remain high for longer average generations (median completion length +45%).
- Latency: median P95 per-token latency increased ~18% on the busy route; bulk of tail latency aligns with longer sequences and concurrent spikes.
- Cost: estimated incremental spend if trend continues: ~$92k/month above current committed baseline.

Options to consider (short):
1) Short-term burst credits + autoscale: keep hosted tier, add 200k burst tokens per month for 3 months (fastest to provision).
2) Mid-term: uplift commit by 50% and move the heavy route to a dedicated model variant with optimized quantization — lower $/token by ~22% (per my calc).
3) Optimization tooling: enable prefix caching for repeated prompts and move image preprocessing client-side to trim tokenized input.

I've included a proposed term-flex draft (proposed-term-flex-commit.xlsx) with a 12-18 month commit ladder and a canary plan for the dedicated route. Marissa, looping you to propose pricing/discount bands and operational rollout.

Next steps: can we do a 30-minute call tomorrow to run the numbers with procurement? If procurement needs an action list, I can push a short mutual action plan before the call.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive — Renewals, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Sanjay Mehra <sanjay@starlift.ai>
Cc: Maya Patel <procurement@starlift.ai>
Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Usage spike ahead of renewal — quick sync?

Thanks Lauren — diving in, attaching a quick latency sample (latency_cpu_gpu_sample.csv) to support the dedicated-vs-hosted comparison. Sanjay / Maya — a pragmatic path we've used for similar customers: 

- Immediate (0–3 weeks): Approve a 3-month burst credit tranche (we propose 200k tokens/month) so production isn't throttled while we finalize the commit. This preserves SLA and gives your engineers breathing room.
- Short (4–8 weeks): 50% uplift on annual commit with a 10% step discount on the extra volume; we validate end-to-end with a 2-week canary on a Dedicated pool (matched GPU family).
- Medium (positioning for cost): If committed uplift proves stable, we convert the canary traffic to a dedicated model variant with 4-bit quantization and prefix caching. Expected net $/token reduction: 20–26% depending on sequence length.

ROI back-of-envelope (based on current Q2 run-rate): 
- Incremental monthly spend avoiding burst credits by moving to the uplifted commit: ~$70k/month saved vs purely burst strategy in month 1–3.
- One-time migration effort:~ 10 engineer-days (placement, smoke tests, telemetry).

I've sketched pricing bands in the attached sheet. If procurement is OK with a short canary + commit uplift, I can generate an amendment draft that preserves existing term dates but adds the new commit ladder and a rollback/fallback clause.

Would tomorrow 10am PT for a 30-min sync work for you both?

—Marissa
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Sanjay Mehra <sanjay@starlift.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <procurement@starlift.ai>, support@starlift.ai
Date: Thu, 20 Jun 2028 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Usage spike ahead of renewal — quick sync?

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Lauren & Marissa. The numbers look reasonable and procurement is especially keen on the canary + commit uplift route so we don't overpay on burst credits. A few quick asks before our sync:

1) Can you send a one-page SLA/rollback blurb for the amendment (we want clear RTO/RPO and fallback to hosted models during canary failures).
2) Please confirm the expected timeline to provision a dedicated pool (engineering ETA).
3) For the ROI calc: can you add a conservative scenario where peak sustained growth is 4x (we want to see downside economics).

We'll take 10am PT tomorrow — I put Maya on the invite. If you can circulate the amendment skeleton beforehand that'd be perfect.

Thanks,
Sanjay
